translations.text: He who revealed this light granted me life, and brought forth that brightness, generously revealed it.
Then I was roused with abundance; the world sprang up [?], spread out under the heavens, covered over with the power of counsel.
I had high rank; there was no lack for me in the hall, so that a brave troop [?] rode there. Often a man there found that he saw in the hall a weight of treasure, a benefit [?] for thanes.
While I had strength, bold men praised me, rescued me in battle, carried me in honour, defended me from enemies.

So a joyful gift held me, a devoted retinue surrounded me; I ruled [?] with landed possessions, I had power over stepping-paths [?], as the earth brought forth; I possessed a lord's throne, I sang with words of song.
The joy of kinship did not fail, but it was a steadfast year; the harp-string [?] rang out, the lasting covenant cut off the stream [?] of sorrow [?].
Servants were keen, the harp was shrill [?], it resounded loudly, the sound rang out, music made melody and did not greatly diminish.

The castle-hall shook, brightness towered up, courage grew, wealth beckoned, it gave wisdom [?] to lords, did good to the bold; the mind grew strong, rejoiced in love [?], trust branched out, glory grew rich, prosperity rejoiced, gold was made ready, gems went round, treasure was skilfully wrought [?], kinship drew close [?].
Now my heart is troubled, fearful of sorrowful journeys, close to dire troubles; he who before was dear in the day departs at night in flight.

The race of men passes away, the slaughter-spear tears, the evil deceiver [?] contends, the arrow is sharpened [?], care for pledges [?] bites, the bold one is whittled away by age [?], the time of exile twists [?], wrath defiles the oath [?], great sorrow [?] spreads,

deceit-craft [?] glides away, fierce grief digs, the grave holds [?], what was cunningly white grows dirty [?], summer heat cools, the wealth of the land falls, enmity wells up, the might of the earth grows old, courage cools.

Fate wove that for me, and my deeds gave me this, that I [dig?] a grave in the ground, and the flesh cannot flee that grim grave when the arrow-swift day seizes me with the grip of necessity, when the night comes which begrudges me my homeland and denies me a dwelling here.

Before that [?] the blessed man considers this: he afflicts himself the more often, buries the bitter sins from himself, sets his mind on the better joy, remembers the grace of rewards [?], where there is the bliss of mercies, full of hope, in the kingdom of the heavens.
